record_type_quote: Our research aims to assess the offer framing effect with two studies utilizing different product categories (replication) and two studies focusing on prosocial product attributes (extension).

targets.authors: Mittelman, M., Andrade, E. B., Chattopadhyay, A., & Brendl, C. M.
targets.title: The Offer Framing Effect: Choosing Single versus Bundled Offerings Affects Variety Seeking.
targets.evidence_quote:
In Study 1a (product category: iced tea), the observed results contradict the original offer framing effect documented by Mittelman et al. (
2014
) and support the findings of O’Donnell et al. (
2023
). Study 1b confirms this direction of effect for a different product category (ice cream). The results of Studies 2a and 2b replicate Study 1’s findings in that participants in the bundled offering condition show a higher preference for variety compared to those in the single offering condition while using prosocial instead of hedonic product attributes. Taken together, we find clear evidence for a higher preference for variety when offered bundled products, with significant results in three out of four studies (Table
1
outlines the chi-square test results for all studies).

targets.authors: O’Donnell, M., Critcher, C. R., & Nelson, L. D.
targets.title: Bundle Selection and Variety Seeking: The Importance of Combinatorics.
targets.evidence_quote: To clarify the direction of effect, we conducted four studies in two product categories and found evidence of a stronger preference for variety in bundled offering conditions (compared to single offering conditions), replicating O’Donnell et al.’s (2023) findings.
